title: Stroke
description: A stroke may affect movement, balance, speech, language, cognition, swallowing, vision, and everyday independence. Rehabilitation is organized around the particular functions that changed.
review_note: Working clinical copy and page model

title: Traumatic Brain Injury
description: A traumatic brain injury may affect physical ability, thinking, communication, behavior, endurance, and participation in daily life. Care should be individualized to the person’s current needs and goals.
review_note: Working clinical copy and page model

title: Spinal Cord Injury
description: Spinal cord injury can affect movement, sensation, mobility, self-care, endurance, and participation. Rehabilitation may focus on safe mobility, adaptive strategies, equipment, and practical independence.
review_note: Working clinical copy and page model

title: Parkinson’s Disease & Movement Disorders
description: Movement disorders may affect walking, balance, coordination, speech, voice, swallowing, and the speed or ease of everyday tasks.
review_note: Working clinical copy and page model

title: Multiple Sclerosis & Progressive Neurological Conditions
description: Progressive neurological conditions may cause changing difficulties with mobility, fatigue, balance, cognition, communication, or daily activity. Rehabilitation can adapt over time.
review_note: Working clinical copy and page model

title: Cerebral Palsy & Pediatric Neurological Conditions
description: Pediatric neurological conditions may affect movement, coordination, posture, communication, feeding, sensory processing, and participation in home and school routines.

title: Balance Disorders, Dizziness & Fall Risk
description: Balance problems may come from neurological, vestibular, strength, medication, vision, or environmental factors. Evaluation identifies the functional problems that should guide treatment.
